item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Wake Forest continues to reach lofty levels in the college football world. With the Demon Deacons beating Georgia Tech 50-29 in Atlanta on Saturday afternoon, Wake is now 10-1 overall and 7-1 in ACC play. The Deacs have assured themselves a spot in the ACC championship game in two weeks in Charlotte. So let’s see what Wake Forest said after the Georgia Tech win. What Wake Forest Said Jake Dickert The head coach said after the game that the locker room celebration was more muted than usual. Wake gave up 249 yards of offense to the Yellowjackets in the second half and was outscored 22-14. “When you look at the totality of the win, I thought it was a good win,” Dickert said after the game. “It’s the first time we have lost a half of football in a long time,” he added, referring back to the first half against Miami on September 18 th . He said the mood after the game has as much to do with the standards of the program now and what the players’ expectations are for themselves. Still, he said, a win is a win. “Don’t undersell winning on the road.” He pointed out that Wake has won six games on the road against Power 4 programs, something Wake claims is a record in the CFP era. The best we could find during that timeframe was other teams that had won five. item.title: UCLA Coach Makes Eye-Opening Bryce Underwood Admission After Michigan Upset
item.description: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood has taken plenty of criticism this season, but following Saturday’s stunning 18-16 triple-overtime victory over No. 4 UCLA, he received some major praise from an unexpected source. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney didn’t hesitate when asked about Michigan’s performance following the Bruins’ first loss of the season. In fact, Chesney had some particularly encouraging words about the Wolverines’ sophomore quarterback. “I thought Bryce [Underwood] had an unbelievable day today,” Chesney said during his postgame press conference . “I thought he threw some balls in some tight windows, including that last play.” That’s a pretty strong endorsement from a coach whose defense had been among the nation’s toughest to score against. Nov 21, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; UCLA head coach Bob Chesney talks with Line Judge Sergio DeHoyos during the first quarter against Michigan at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bryce Underwood Earns Respect After Difficult Stretch Underwood’s performance wasn’t exactly eye-popping statistically, as he completed 11 of 24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown. However, he delivered when Michigan needed him most, connecting with Jalen Hoffman on the game-winning two-point conversion in the third overtime. The performance was especially meaningful considering Underwood’s recent struggles and the quarterback controversy surrounding Michigan’s offense. After losing his starting job earlier this season , Underwood returned to the starting lineup against the previously undefeated Bruins and helped deliver Michigan’s biggest victory of the year. According to the official UCLA game recap , the Bruins entered Saturday with a perfect 10-0 record. Underwood’s decisive completion ended that unbeaten run and improved Michigan to 6-5, making the Wolverines bowl eligible. Chesney also credited Michigan’s physical defense and the toughness of the Wolverines’ overall performance. Still, his praise for Underwood stood out because UCLA had held Michigan to just 247 total yards and fewer than 50 percent completions. With Michigan preparing for its rivalry showdown against Ohio State , Underwood still has plenty to prove. But after everything he has experienced this season, hearing that kind of praise from the opposing head coach has to feel pretty good. And for Michigan fans hoping Underwood can become the quarterback they envisioned, Saturday was a much-needed step in the right direction.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama Throws Shade At NBA Stars After 50-Point Game: “I’m Not Very Good At Stat Padding”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama delivered a playful jab at his NBA peers after scoring 50 points in the San Antonio Spurs ’ 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday, suggesting his approach to individual statistics has limited his milestone performances . The Spurs superstar finished with 19 rebounds, five blocks, four steals, and one assist alongside his scoring outburst. He shot 20-of-29 from the field and 5-of-11 from three-point range, producing a dominant performance in just 32 minutes. “It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding. So I haven’t reached it as many times as I should have.” Wembanyama did not identify anyone as the target of that remark. However, the comment added another layer to a remarkable night that helped San Antonio improve to 14-3, matching the NBA’s best record. This was his second 50-point performance of the season and the third of his career. He previously scored a career-high 52 against the Dallas Mavericks on November 4. His latest effort tied David Robinson for the second-most 50-point games in Spurs history, behind George Gervin’s five. Wembanyama established control early, scoring 17 first-quarter points before reaching halftime with 32 points and 13 rebounds. The Spurs led 61-45 at the break, with their centerpiece influencing the game at both ends. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. “That step-back three that I took, it doesn’t correlate with this. It didn’t fit the definition, for example. So I did try, at the end, yeah, I did try to get a three when I had 47 points.” That admission gave his earlier remark an amusing contradiction. Wembanyama had teased others about chasing numbers, then openly conceded that he wanted the extra three points himself. He defended that instinct by referencing Wilt Chamberlain . “I don’t think Wilt thought about that when he had 98 points. I don’t think he thought about making the extra pass.” There is a reasonable distinction between enjoying a milestone and compromising a team’s chances to reach one. Wembanyama’s scoring came with exceptional efficiency, overwhelming rebounding, and substantial defensive production in a comfortable victory. His contribution extended far beyond the points column. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson also acknowledged that removing him just short of 50 would have been difficult, while emphasizing the importance of avoiding unnecessary injury risk. Ultimately, Wembanyama gave fans both a spectacular performance and a memorable sound bite. The stat-padding remark invited debate, but his willingness to admit chasing the final basket kept it from becoming a simple lecture directed at everyone else. At 22, he is already producing nights that require very little embellishment.

item.title: ESPN icon, Broncos legend Tom Jackson passes away at 75
item.description: The NFL and sports media worlds are in mourning, following the shocking news that Denver Broncos legend and ESPN icon Tom Jackson has passed away at age 75. The news was announced at the start of Sunday NFL Countdown ahead of Week 11. At the request of Jackson’s family, an emotional Chris Berman fought through tears to deliver the news while reading a statement. “All of us are stunned,” Berman said in a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned, and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet , Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown . “We’ve lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet.” Chris Berman announces the death of his longtime broadcast partner and best friend, Tom Jackson. What an iconic duo for all those years. Thank you, TJ ❤️ https://t.co/0eogqMa73r — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 22, 2026 “It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.” An official cause of death has not been announced at this time. Tom Jackson Was A Trail Blazer Sep 14, 2015; Atlanta, GA, USA; ESPN broadcaster Tom Jackson smiles prior to the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Atlanta Falcons at the Georgia Dome. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Before becoming a household name on ESPN, Jackson was a vaunted defender and member of the Broncos’ “Orange Crush” defense. As a player, Jackson was a fourth-round pick in 1973 out of Louisville, before becoming a two-time Pro Bowl during his 14 years with the Broncos. As an analyst, he was once again among the best, becoming a Hall of Fame broadcaster. Jackson retired from ESPN in 2016 after his final assignment, the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement ceremony alongside Berman. Berman said, “Tom long ago became almost a brother to me. I know every day he appeared on ESPN was a treasure for football fans.” Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and his two daughters, Taylor and Morgan. item.title: Did beaten Wales still show they have come a long way?
item.description: Wales won three Tests at Principality Stadium in 2026 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] For experienced hooker Ryan Elias, the proof of Wales' progress came when he looked around in the post-match huddle and saw heads down after a narrow defeat by Australia. Steve Tandy's side failed to back up their historic victory against New Zealand when edged out 28-25 by the Wallabies in the Nations Championship. Wales could not claim another scalp against the Aussies, who are two places above them in seventh in World Rugby's rankings, but went close. "It wasn't that long ago, not even 12 months ago, that we probably would have been chuffed with that result," said 54-times capped Scarlets forward Elias. "You look around the circle at the end of that game and there were boys with heads down because this is one that got away. "That just shows the growth of the group and the belief that's coming." Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat Wales should have picked Botham, says flanker's dad Next Sunday is the one-year anniversary of Wales' 73-0 defeat by South Africa in Cardiff, a hammering that was followed by heavy Six Nations losses against England and France. Tandy's squad have since enjoyed victories against Italy, Fiji and Japan before the statement success against New Zealand. "It's hard to recreate what they did against the All Blacks," former Wales centre Tom Shanklin said on Scrum V podcast. "It's hard to get to that level every week but it was really positive. We're still in a building phase. "We said the best thing about the Japan game was that it was a bonus-point win, and that was about it. "That feels a long time ago. We've come a long, long way. "The effort was there against Australia, but there just wasn't that clinical edge and maybe that's a psychological thing." Wales were nervy 28-21 winners at the start of November against a Japan side who have since been thumped by England and Scotland. They face the Brave Blossoms again on Saturday (13:10 GMT) at Nations Championship finals weekend at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. "This is a big game now to see how much we've changed and developed from the first game of the campaign to the last," said Shanklin. Sherratt sharpening up Wales' attack Wales chalked up four-try bonuses in all three games in Cardiff and have added to their threat from driving line-out. They have profited from consistency at 10-12-13 with Sam Costelow, Max Llewellyn and Eddie James. "You're seeing a team that seems to have found an attack," said Shanklin. "Matt Sherratt has worked really hard with them and we've got various options now, we're not too predictable. "We're playing with a lot more quick ball and we're quite clever in how we're breaking teams down. "There are multiple options now when taking the ball to the line and we are getting it into the hands of our strike runners." Wales did, however, waste a number of 22 entries in the first half and the final try by Ryan Elias came after pressure that ate into the clock. "

item.title: Eric DeCosta Is Officially On the Hot Seat
item.description: General Manager Eric DeCosta has failed to build a complete team around Lamar Jackson . The Baltimore Ravens have reached a point where their problems can no longer be blamed on one injury or one bad performance. Their recent 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers exposed a roster with too many weaknesses. Baltimore started off the season with a 4-1 record, but they’re now sitting at 4-6. Jackson’s absence has certainly hurt the offense. But a team that’s built to contend for a Super Bowl should not completely fall apart when its franchise quarterback can’t play. The Ravens have struggled to run the ball and protect their other four quarterbacks while also not being able to stop opposing offenses. These problems raise serious questions about DeCosta and the way he has constructed this roster. Baltimore has invested heavily in established players, but a majority of those investments have not produced the expected results. DeCosta has had multiple years to address certain weaknesses, yet the same problems continue to hurt the team. The Ravens Cannot Function Without Lamar Jackson The biggest concern with Baltimore’s roster is how dependent the team has become on Jackson. His absence has exposed how little the offense can accomplish without him. Before Jacoby Brissett ‘s start, Baltimore averaged 103.4 yards per quarter with Jackson on the field, compared to just 67.6 without him. Jackson has already dealt with multiple injuries this season. He suffered an ankle injury against Tennessee and a thumb injury against Buffalo that required surgery. Even with Jackson under contract through 2027, Baltimore cannot keep putting him in spots where he has to carry the roster year after year. The remaining players must be capable of producing when he is unavailable. DeCosta deserves criticism for failing to build enough depth around Jackson. A roster with championship expectations should have more answers when its starting quarterback goes down. Eric DeCosta Has Failed to Fix the Offensive Line The offensive line has been Baltimore’s biggest concern for multiple seasons. Despite repeated attempts to address the position, the unit continues to struggle. They kept putting Jackson in tough situations. In fact, Tyler Huntley is now out for the season after being sacked. In addition to being ineffective in pass protection, the team has also faced problems with the running game. Going into Week 9, the Ravens offensive line had seen 25 different combinations of players, which was the highest in the NFL at that point in time. Though some of the changes can be attributed to injuries, it shows how difficult it has been to assemble a reliable group. item.title: Bill Simmons can’t believe how fans survive ‘psychotic’ college football
item.description: Photo by Mike Windle/Getty Images for Vanity Fair Bill Simmons has not been into college football for too long and he is already feeling the pressure. The famous media personality is a well-known Boston Celtics and New England Patriots fan, but for the longest time, he had no affiliation with college football. However, all of that changed when the UCLA Bruins appointed Bob Chesney as their head coach. Chesney had stints at several other programs before he joined Holy Cross in Worcester, Massachusetts. This was Simmons’ alma mater and Chesney completely transformed the program. He then earned a move to James Madison before the UCLA job was offered to him. Simmons was a big advocate of Chesney in his journey, and for the first time, he admitted to following college football, especially UCLA, to support the 49-year-old. In his very first season following college football, Simmons is finding things a little difficult, as the Bruins had an intense matchup against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday. Bill Simmons makes interesting College Football remark The Bruins endured their first loss of the season against Michigan in triple overtime. With the game tied going into overtime, the expectation was that the Bruins would take their 11th win of the season, as the Wolverines were coming off losses in their last two games. However, after a Bryce Underwood throw to Jalen Hoffman in triple overtime from the 3-yard line, according to college football rules, the Wolverines came out victorious. Regardless of the result, it was an intense game. “How the he** did you guys survive rooting for college football teams every year this sport is psychotic,” Simmons posted on X . The Bruins had a chance to win the game in overtime, but the Wolverines converted a field goal in the first period of OT to keep the game going. Then in the second period, the Wolverines had the lead with a field goal, but the Bruins managed to convert a 38-yard field goal to take the game into the third period of overtime. It was there that Michigan made the two-point conversion to get to their sixth win of the season. While their CFP dreams are likely over, they have a chance to end their season on a high note with a win against Ohio State. Meanwhile, the Bruins will be looking to respond strongly to the defeat as they take on USC in their final game of the regular season. item.title: Bruno Fernandes confirms Man Utd contract offer but says he’ll leave if it's the right time
item.description: Bruno Fernandes confirms Man Utd contract offer but says he’ll leave if it's the right time Bruno Fernandes has revealed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but said he's prepared to leave if all parties decide it's the right time. Fernandes's current contract expires at the end of the season, though United hold an option to extend his deal until 2028. The 32-year-old was named PFA Player of the Year in 2025/26 after breaking the Premier League 's single-season assist record, but has been part of a struggling side this season. United are 19th in the Premier League table ahead of facing Liverpool this afternoon, in what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge. The Argentine has replaced Michael Carrick following the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. Ahead of that game, Fernandes said he has rejected multiple offers to leave Manchester in recent summers and outlined his commitment to the club. However, he said now is not the time to discuss a new deal with the focus on improving results. "I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester," he said to Sky Sports. "Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on. "I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door. "Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

item.title: Tom Izzo Unloads on NCAA Over Detroit Mercy Punishment
item.description: Michigan State head coach Tom Izzo wasn’t holding back following the Spartans’ 91-70 victory over Detroit Mercy on Saturday afternoon. But his frustration had nothing to do with his team’s performance. Instead, Izzo took aim at the NCAA over its punishment of Detroit Mercy and head coach Mark Montgomery, a former Michigan State player and longtime Izzo assistant. “The APR is a joke,” Izzo said during his postgame press conference . “You can’t have an APR when kids are allowed to leave whenever they want.” Izzo’s frustration stems from penalties handed down to Detroit Mercy after the program failed to meet the NCAA’s Academic Progress Rate (APR) requirements. Those penalties include a postseason ban for the 2026-27 season and restrictions on practice time. Michigan State’s men’s basketball coach Tom Izzo yells during a men’s college basketball game between Tennessee and Michigan State at Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center on Nov. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Izzo Defends His Former Assistant Izzo believes Montgomery is being punished for academic problems that developed before he took over the program. He was particularly upset that the sanctions went beyond postseason eligibility and affected how often the Titans could practice. According to Detroit Mercy’s official announcement , the program failed to reach the required APR benchmark of 930. Izzo’s criticism comes as he has repeatedly questioned the impact of the transfer portal and the NCAA’s approach to regulating college athletics. He has also challenged recent NCAA eligibility decisions . For Izzo, however, Saturday’s criticism was personal. Montgomery played for Michigan State from 1988-92 and later spent years on Izzo’s coaching staff. The Spartans improved to 5-1 with Saturday’s victory, but Izzo made sure the conversation didn’t end with the final score. His former assistant’s situation clearly struck a nerve, and the NCAA was squarely in his sights.

item.title: Packers Sign Familiar Face Amid Josh Jacobs Injury Questions

(Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers. Getty Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs returned to practice on Saturday. However, head coach Matt LaFleur does not anticipate Jacobs playing in the team’s Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Rams unless something substantially changes with his finger. As a response, the Packers re-signed veteran running back Pierre Strong to the practice squad. They released edge rusher D.J. Johnson as the corresponding move. Strong has been active for the Packers for five games this season. Green Bay Packers Sign Pierre Strong Back to Practice Squad Getty Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers. The injuries in the running back room led to Strong having a role early on in the season. Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner’s exempt list, and then shortly after that Chris Brooks was placed on the IR. Because Kaleb Johnson was just acquired in a trade before the season started, he was slow to get onto the field as well. So the team relied on strong early in the season. Strong has mostly been a passing-down weapon, so he only has 25 carries this season, but has 114 snaps played. Despite playing 30 snaps in Week 9, he was a healthy scratch in Week 10 when the team brought Brooks back. Johnson had started to ascend as the lead back and the team still is not giving up on third-round pick MarShawn Lloyd. Beyond that, he is still on his rookie salary, so the team would have to see him clear waivers. Strong is a journeyman who’s been on three teams in five seasons. He was only brought in because the team lacked depth and needed some help. So he was more likely to clear waivers than Lloyd. With Brooks back into the mix, the team did not have a significant need for a strong either, so if he did end up getting claimed on waivers, it would not have been a big loss. Packers Add Strong Back to Practice Squad The news is likely not good for the status of Jacobs playing in Week 11. Green Bay will lean on Johnson, with Lloyd as the backup and Brooks as the third-down back. Adding Strong is depth because they do not plan to have any with Jacobs out. Now that he has re-signed with the team, they can use three practice squad elevations on him before they have to decide to bring him back onto the active roster. If Jacobs is out, they have a chance to use one of them on Strong in Week 12. Releasing Johnson is a good sign that Micah Parsons will be back this week, as the team does not need depth on the edge anymore. Green Bay faces the Rams in Week 12. We will see if Strong gets called up and if Jacobs is active. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Packers Sign Familiar Face Amid Josh Jacobs Injury Questions

item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes (Glyn KIRK) Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has revealed it is "not the right time" for talks over a new contract with his troubled club. Fernandes's future at Old Trafford has been a source of constant doubt in recent years and the speculation that he is ready to quit United continues to swirl. With his current deal due to expire at the end of the season, the 32-year-old has turned down a second offer of a new contract. Fernandes snubbed the chance to move to Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal in the close-season, but with United in turmoil this term, he is not ready to reopen contract talks with the club he joined in 2020. "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay," Fernandes told Sky Sports on Sunday. "There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. "I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. "Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. "I've always showed how much I care about this club and how much I want to win at this club. I've always said, the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on." The Portugal midfielder's form has dipped this season and he has only managed one goal and assist since his hat-trick against Ipswich in August. Fernandes was dropped by Michael Carrick earlier this season after criticising his tactics. Carrick has since been sacked, with Mauricio Pochettino hired to lift United away from the relegation zone. Often criticised for his emotional outbursts and body language on the pitch, Fernandes is keeping his focus on United's cause for now as they start a new era under former USA coach Pochettino. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract," Fernandes said. "But about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations. item.title: Unlikely heroes in TE room fire Michigan Football to upset win bs UCLA
item.description: I don’t believe it. You probably don’t either. But it’s happened. The unranked Michigan football team, mired in a season shaped by disappointment and mockery, has beaten an undefeated, top-five team in the country. The Wolverines stunned No. 4 UCLA, 18-16 in triple overtime. And they did it off the backs of a position group that hasn’t been at its best all year long. Michigan has lacked a tight end capable of shouldering the offense this season for the first time in years. Following the steady play of Marlin Klein and Colston Loveland, the Wolverines rolled out a more ragtag array in 2026, led by Hogan Hansen and Jalen Hoffman. But that group stepped up on Saturday, delivering both of Michigan’s scoring plays in its most stunning victory of the year. “I’ll tell you what, Mason Bonner did some good things tonight as well, and he’s a tight end technically,” head coach Kyle Whittingham said. “He’s played mostly, flexed out in wide receiver … but those guys have been great contributors. Hogan Hansen’s contributed throughout the season as well…” After three relatively tepid quarters, it was Bonner who broke open the scoring. With a clean pocket, Underwood was able to find Bonner right into the end zone to his left, who made a hugely impressive one-handed grab for the score. It was the freshman’s first receiving touchdown of his career, and though a boom-or-bust outing — three grabs for 47 yards and the touchdown — he certainly made a mark. The other tight end to make a mark didn’t actually record a single reception on the stats sheet. Yet his play was the game-winner. With the game into triple overtime and Michigan needing a successful two-point conversion to win, Hoffman, a former walk-on and senior who had recorded zero receptions in his first three seasons, practically ripped the ball out of the defensive back’s hands for the win — a Hollywood moment. “I’m just proud of that room,” Hoffman said. “And we’ve all went through a lot, virtually the whole team’s went through a lot. We kept working, kept fighting, and when opportunities came, we made plays.” All year long, the Wolverines’ tight ends room hasn’t been the crux of the offense. The position group’s statistical leader is Hansen with just 128 yards. Even in a highly dysfunctional year of offense for Michigan, the burden has been shouldered by the receiving room, as injured wideout JJ Buchanan has captured the lions’ share of yards and targets. But that didn’t matter on Saturday — because when Michigan needed help, it got it from two unlikely heroes.

item.description: Kimi Antonelli has admitted his own battery management mistake on the last lap of the Las Vegas Grand Prix "compromised" his chance at victory against Max Verstappen . Hoping to attack the Dutchman on Lap 50 in Sin City, the Italian was instead "smoked by the McLarens" and finished fourth. Despite going quickest in Las Vegas GP Qualifying, Antonelli started the race from P6 after taking a five-place engine penalty, but was fighting for the win in the closing stages of a race featuring a total of 352 overtakes. 35 of those passes were for the lead, and while most were between fierce rivals Verstappen and Antonelli's Mercedes teammate George Russell, the new world champion became the closest challenger to the Red Bull driver with 12 laps to go before Russell's crash at Lap 48 when trying to pass Antonelli. Last-lap battery blunder costs Antonelli Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures With Mercedes and Red Bull working on figuring out the best battery management strategy in anticipation of a last-lap shootout to the line, Antonelli explained where it all went wrong, and how he became vulnerable to McLaren duo Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri behind him. The 20-year-old told Sky F1 : "I think the change of deployment was good because it was the best option to then stay ahead after the chicane in case I was overtaking Max before turn 14. "But because I wanted to keep the overtake mode, I lifted off and reapplied some throttle to keep a little bit of speed, and that messed up the whole battery harvesting, and at the chicane I had zero. "So I lost more than a second going into Turn 1 and, not only couldn't stay close to Max and give myself a good shot for the win, I got smoked by the two McLarens as well and lost the podium. "So probably was a mistake on my side but in the moment it is also very difficult because I thought I was doing something right to stay behind and keep the overtake [mode] but turned it compromised the race." As F1's youngest ever champion explains, the hope was to avoid "forcing anything" and preserve overtake mode for an attack in the final corners. In the end, it was not to be, but the 20-year-old still managed to have some fun during what was an exciting race. "My goal, my objective, was to stay behind all the way to the end," he said.
